definition: Separating a music mix into stems — vocals, drums, bass — a task led by models like Demucs for remixing and analysis.
details: Separating a music mix into stems — vocals, drums, bass — a task led by models like Demucs for remixing and analysis.

explainer.lead: Music source separation splits a music mix into stems — vocals, drums, bass — with models like Demucs leading the task. It matters for remixing, karaoke, and analysis of existing recordings.

tiers.eli5: Like pulling apart a smoothie back into its separate fruits — here, pulling a song into vocals, drums, and bass.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers run waveform or spectrogram models that output one stem per source, often training on synthetic mixes made by summing isolated stems. A pitfall is bleed and artefacts on unusual instrumentation not represented in training data.
tiers.paperLevel: Estimate each source signal from the mixture, typically by minimising reconstruction error between predicted stems and ground-truth isolated stems. Quality degrades when sources overlap heavily in time and frequency.

explainer.example: A stereo track is run through Demucs, yielding separate vocal and drum files used to build a karaoke version.
